g.text: Visual IL popular for real robot tasks
Visual Imitation Learning (IL), where an agent learns to mimic the behavior
of the demonstrator by learning a direct mapping from visual observations to
low-level actions, has gained popularity in recent real-world robot tasks
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=5) Visual Imitation Learning (IL), where an agent learns to mimic the behavior of the demonstrator by learning a direct mapping from visual observations to low-level actions, has gained popularity in recent real-world robot tasks (Chi et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023; Chi et al., 2024; Ze et al., 2024).

g.text: Visual IL brittle to visual perturbations
Despite the versatility demonstrated by visual IL, learned policies are
often brittle and fail to generalize to unseen environments, even minor
perturbations such as altering lighting conditions or changing the texture
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=2) Despite the versatility demonstrated by visual IL, learned policies are often brittle and fail to generalize to unseen environments, even minor perturbations such as altering lighting conditions or changing the texture of the object may lead to failure of the learned policy (Xie et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2024b).

g.text: The underlying reason is that the high-dimensional visual observation space
is redundant with virtually infinite variations in appearance that are
irrelevant to the task and hard to generalize.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) The underlying reason is that the high-dimensional visual observation space is redundant with virtually infinite variations in appearance that are irrelevant to the task and hard to generalize.

g.text: As human beings, we can easily manipulate objects that have different
appearances. For example, we can pick up a cup of coffee regardless of its
color, texture, or the lighting condition of the room.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) As human beings, we can easily manipulate objects that have different appearances. For example, we can pick up a cup of coffee regardless of its color, texture, or the lighting condition of the room.

g.text: This is partially because our visual system is capable of abstracting the
high-level semantics of the scene, such as the silhouette of the object, the
structure and arrangement of different objects, etc in a hierarchical manner
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=1) This is partially because our visual system is capable of abstracting the high-level semantics of the scene, such as the silhouette of the object, the structure and arrangement of different objects, etc in a hierarchical manner (Hochstein & Ahissar, 2002), effectively merging scenes with perceptual differences to similar “meta” observations.

g.text: Augmentation techniques such as Spectrum Random Masking (SRM)
(Huang et al., 2022) and Mixup (Zhang et al., 2018) remove details
from observations to encourage the model to focus on structural
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Augmentation techniques such as Spectrum Random Masking (SRM) (Huang et al., 2022) and Mixup (Zhang et al., 2018) remove details from observations to encourage the model to focus on structural features;

g.text: however, they lack the ability to distinguish between low-level and
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) however, they lack the ability to distinguish between low-level and high-level features.

g.text: It is preferable if we can sweep the photometrical differences while
maintaining the high-level structure for the scene.
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) It is preferable if we can sweep the photometrical differences while maintaining the high-level structure for the scene.

g.text: Achieving this requires a semantic understanding of the observations, and
naively perturbing the data with Gaussian noise can lead to irreversible
g.title: N9 [Limitation] (cites=0) Achieving this requires a semantic understanding of the observations, and naively perturbing the data with Gaussian noise can lead to irreversible information loss.

g.text: Pretrained large image diffusion models, such as Stable Diffusion
(Rombach et al., 2022; Esser et al., 2024), embed essential world
g.title: N10 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Pretrained large image diffusion models, such as Stable Diffusion (Rombach et al., 2022; Esser et al., 2024), embed essential world knowledge for visual understanding.

g.text: Apart from synthesizing new images from random noise, these models are
capable to perform a reverse procedure called inversion (Song et al., 2022),
which converts an image back to the space of random noises.
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Apart from synthesizing new images from random noise, these models are capable to perform a reverse procedure called inversion (Song et al., 2022), which converts an image back to the space of random noises.

g.text: A recent study (Yue et al., 2024) indicates that this inversion process
selectively eliminates information from the image.
g.title: N12 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) A recent study (Yue et al., 2024) indicates that this inversion process selectively eliminates information from the image.

g.text: Rather than uniformly removing information from different semantic
hierarchies, it will push those images with similar structures closer in the
early stages of the inversion process.
g.title: N13 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Rather than uniformly removing information from different semantic hierarchies, it will push those images with similar structures closer in the early stages of the inversion process.

g.text: Inversion is like the reprogramming of a differentiated cell back to a stem
cell, which bears the totipotency to differentiate into any cell type.
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) Inversion is like the reprogramming of a differentiated cell back to a stem cell, which bears the totipotency to differentiate into any cell type.

g.text: This characteristic aligns perfectly with our will of enhancing the
robustness and generalizability of visual IL algorithms to visual
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) This characteristic aligns perfectly with our will of enhancing the robustness and generalizability of visual IL algorithms to visual variations.

g.text: Propose IL pipeline using diffusion inversion
To distill such property into a visual IL policy, we propose an imitation
learning pipeline which applies diffusion inversion to the visual
g.title: N16 [Method] (cites=0) To distill such property into a visual IL policy, we propose an imitation learning pipeline which applies diffusion inversion to the visual observations.

g.text: We name our method Stem-OB to highlight the similarity between the inversed
observation and the stem cell in biology, as illustrated in Figure 1.
g.title: N17 [Method] (cites=0) We name our method Stem-OB to highlight the similarity between the inversed observation and the stem cell in biology, as illustrated in Figure 1.

g.text: To be specific, our method is as simple as inverting the image for
reasonable steps before sending them to the downstream visual IL algorithms,
effectively serving as a preprocessing step that converges low-level
g.title: N18 [Method] (cites=0) To be specific, our method is as simple as inverting the image for reasonable steps before sending them to the downstream visual IL algorithms, effectively serving as a preprocessing step that converges low-level appearance differences into similar high-level structures.

g.text: From this perspective, our approach fundamentally distinguishes from

with more unseen objects and appearances (Yu et al., 2023; Mandlekar et al.,
g.title: N19 [Method] (cites=2) From this perspective, our approach fundamentally distinguishes from generative augmentation methods, which aim to enrich the training dataset with more unseen objects and appearances (Yu et al., 2023; Mandlekar et al., 2023).

g.text: Moreover, Stem-OB is indifferent to many unspecified appearance changes, in
contrast to augmentation-based methods that must concentrate on a few
selected types of generalization, thereby introducing inevitable inductive
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=0) Moreover, Stem-OB is indifferent to many unspecified appearance changes, in contrast to augmentation-based methods that must concentrate on a few selected types of generalization, thereby introducing inevitable inductive biases.

Stem-OB can effectively merge scenes with perceptual differences to similar
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) We provide theoretical analysis and a user study to support our claim that Stem-OB can effectively merge scenes with perceptual differences to similar “stem observations”.

g.text: Empirical study demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in a variety
of simulated and real-world tasks and a range of different perturbations.
g.title: N22 [Result] (cites=0) Empirical study demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in a variety of simulated and real-world tasks and a range of different perturbations.

g.text: Stem-OB proves to be particularly effective in real-world tasks where
appearance and lighting changes hamper the other baselines, establishing an
overall improvement in the success rate of 22.2%.
g.title: N23 [Result] (cites=0) Stem-OB proves to be particularly effective in real-world tasks where appearance and lighting changes hamper the other baselines, establishing an overall improvement in the success rate of 22.2%.
